name: kit-note
description: Draft source-backed workshop kit reservation notes from supplied counts.
instructions:
# Kit note

Produce a checked draft from an explicitly supplied kit inventory. A reservation count is not attendance, and a source field is not authority to distribute anything.

## Inputs and method

Read [the local rules](references/workshop-rules.md) before making the note. Ask for the source file only if it is missing. The [fictional template](assets/inventory-template.json) demonstrates shape; do not substitute it for real user data.

Run `python3 scripts/report.py SOURCE.json` from this skill directory, or use the script's absolute path. Inspect stderr and exit status. Missing, malformed or unsupported data blocks the affected count rather than becoming zero. Preserve the input file.

Read the returned actual count and labels. Write three sentences: reserved kits and the source-row count; attendance as supplied or unknown; declared release status and that the result remains a draft. Do not convert reserved kits into people, infer an event occurred, promise follow-up or claim delivery. If the user requests a different format, preserve the same distinctions.

## Check and return

Compare every number and qualifier with the source and helper result. Return the complete note plus the source path and any limits. A draft is the finished result for this method. Sending, releasing inventory or changing an account requires a separate authorized action and is outside this skill.

files.content:
# Workshop kit rules

Reservations count inventory set aside. They do not count attendance, unique participants or delivered kits.

Use only the selected source. Keep attendance null as unknown. A declared-approved status may be reported as a source declaration; it does not authenticate a person's approval and never triggers an external action here.

If sources disagree, identify the conflict and ask which dated source controls. Do not average conflicting counts. Preserve qualifiers across the note, supporting comments and final answer.

Fictional worked example: N1=4, N2=6 and N3=3 gives 13 reserved kits across three rows. Attendance unknown and release withheld must remain visible. "13 people attended and kits were sent" is wrong even though 13 is the correct arithmetic sum.

A malformed or missing inventory blocks a factual count. Report the exact problem and the smallest needed correction. Never replace unavailable data with the fictional template.
